intro: bgcode to G-code converts Prusa binary G-code (.bgcode) into normal text G-code. It is useful to read or edit the commands, find a layer change, add a pause by hand, check the temperatures or use the file on another printer or in a program that does not understand the binary format.

Blocks are decompressed (Heatshrink or Deflate), MeatPack is unpacked (including the no-space mode, putting back the spaces between parameters) and each block's CRC32 is checked, so a damaged file gives an error instead of a corrupt G-code. Thumbnails and metadata are written back as comments, the way PrusaSlicer puts them in text G-code.

The conversion is our own, built from the specification Prusa publishes, and has been checked against real PrusaSlicer 2.6 and 2.8 files: the commands that come out are identical to the original G-code's. If you later want to go back to the binary format, use G-code to bgcode.
You can convert up to ten files per task. They are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted automatically when they expire.

faq.q: Why is the G-code so much bigger?
faq.a: Because text is not compressed: it is usually two to five times the size of the bgcode.
Yes, as comments at the start of the G-code, in PrusaSlicer's format.

faq.q: What if it says it is damaged?
faq.a: A block fails its CRC32: the file was copied badly. Export or download it again.

faq.q: Can I open the result in PrusaSlicer's viewer?
faq.a: Yes: text G-code opens in PrusaSlicer's G-code viewer and in any other.

faq.q: Can I edit it and turn it back into bgcode?
faq.a: Yes: edit the text and convert it again with G-code to bgcode.
